Metadata.title: Adsum — attendance notebook, no sign-up
Metadata.description: Whoever provides the service notes the days on their own phone and sends the month's summary. The client invites, receives and checks. No sign-up.

About.title: About Adsum
About.intro: Adsum is Latin for “present!”, the answer at roll call. It's a simple attendance notebook with no sign-up, from the Sidekick series by GR1618 Labs.

what.title: What it's for
what.p1: Whoever provides a service notes the days they were on site, with arrival, leaving and a short note. At the end of the month, they send the summary to whoever hired them.
what.p2: The client invites people, receives the summaries, checks them and downloads the spreadsheet to pay. Both sides see the same summary.
what.p3: Adsum is a notebook agreed between the parties. It is not a time clock, does not replace any working-time record required by law, and does not prove any kind of employment relationship.

safety.title: How to tell a real link
safety.p1: Adsum links start with {host}. Adsum never asks for a password, ID, photo or payment.
safety.p2: Be wary of messages asking for any of these in Adsum's name.

notebook.title: Where the notes live
notebook.p1: The notebook of whoever provides the service stays on their own phone. The server receives only what the person chooses to share: the month's summary and, if they want, the day's arrival and leaving notice.
notebook.p2: The day's notices disappear at midnight. Summaries are kept for 60 days after they are sent.

who.title: Who makes it
who.p1: Adsum is made by {operator} as an independent project. It's free, with no ads and no data sales.
who.p2: It's in a pilot with a few people before opening to the public.

code.title: Open source
code.p1: All the code is published at <repo>github.com/pacioli1618-oss/adsum</repo> under the AGPL-3.0 license. Anyone can check what the app does with data.

Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.intro: Adsum keeps as little as possible, for as short as possible. This page explains what, where and for how long.

collect.title: What goes to the server
collect.p1: From the client: the place's name, the agreed rate, the language, the date the terms were accepted and the names used in invites.
collect.p2: From whoever provides the service, only after accepting an invite: each month's summary they send (days, amount and, if they choose, times and notes) and, if they turn it on, the day's arrival and leaving notices.
collect.p3: We don't ask for e-mail, phone, ID, photo or location. There is no sign-up and no password: access is by link.

notebook.title: What stays on the phone
notebook.p1: The notebook of whoever provides the service — every day, time, note and client — stays in the browser storage of their own phone and doesn't go to the server.
notebook.p2: Admin and invite links are also kept on the device, so the app opens without the link again.

visibility.title: Who sees what
visibility.p1: The client sees, for each invited person: whether they accepted, the summaries they sent and, if they turned it on, the day's notices.
visibility.p2: Whoever provides the service sees the place's name, the rate and the check of each summary sent. One person doesn't see the other people at the same place.

retention.title: For how long
retention.p1: Arrival and leaving notices: until the end of the day itself. Summaries: 60 days after they are sent. Places unused for 400 days are erased with everything in them.
retention.p2: The client can delete the place any time. Whoever provides the service can stop sharing any time; that erases the day's notices.

providers.title: Services we use
providers.p1: The app runs on Vercel and the data is stored on Supabase, in the São Paulo region. To limit abuse, we keep for a short time a code derived from the network address, which can't be turned back into the address.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.p1: You can ask for access to, correction or deletion of your data. Since there is no sign-up, the fastest way is the app's own options: delete the place, remove a person, stop sharing or remove a client from the notebook.
rights.p2: For any other request, use the contact below.

controller.title: Controller
controller.p1: {operator} is responsible for the data that reaches the server. The notes agreed between the client and whoever provides the service are the parties' responsibility.

Terms.title: Terms of use
Terms.intro: Short rules for using Adsum. By creating a place or accepting an invite, you agree to them.

service.title: The service
service.p1: Adsum is a free notebook, offered as is, in a pilot phase. It may change, go offline or shut down.
service.p2: Keep your own copies: download each month's spreadsheet.

notRecord.title: Not a time clock
notRecord.p1: Adsum is not an electronic working-time record system, does not meet Brazil's Portaria MTP nº 671/2021 and does not replace any control required by law.
notRecord.p2: The notes are made by whoever provides the service, on their own phone, and can be corrected by that person. They don't prove any kind of employment relationship.

notParty.title: Adsum is not part of the agreement
notParty.p1: The client and whoever provides the service agree between themselves on the work, the rate and the payment. {operator} doesn't intermediate, doesn't receive or pass on payments and isn't liable for what is agreed.

responsibility.title: Each one answers for what they note
responsibility.p1: The client answers for the names and rates they enter. Whoever provides the service answers for the days, times and notes they send.
responsibility.p2: Don't use Adsum to watch people, for illegal purposes or to store sensitive data in notes.

records.title: Keeping the data
records.p1: Summaries stay on the server for 60 days and notices only on the day itself. The notebook stays on the phone of whoever provides the service. If you need to keep them longer, download the spreadsheet.

links.title: Links
links.p1: Whoever has the admin link controls the place; whoever has the invite link controls the sharing. Don't share these links with anyone who shouldn't have them.

license.title: Open source
license.p1: Adsum's code is published under the AGPL-3.0 license at <repo>github.com/pacioli1618-oss/adsum</repo>.

law.title: Governing law
law.p1: These terms are governed by the laws of Brazil.

Install.title: Add to home screen
Install.intro: That way Adsum sits with your apps and opens straight on your notebook.
Install.ios1: Tap the Share button (the square with an arrow pointing up) in Safari's bar.
Install.ios2: Scroll and tap "Add to Home Screen".
Install.ios3: Tap "Add". The Adsum icon shows up on your home screen.
Install.menu1: Open the browser menu (the three dots ⋮).
Install.menu2: Tap "Add to Home screen" or "Install app" and confirm.
